items.name: Chapter 09, Pillar icons

reasons.craft: The rows, the size ladder and the enlarged fits are exact at 1x and 2x, with the 24 px fit on 1x and the master on 2x as DR-179 set; the phone column trails its down arrows after each word at three different x positions.
reasons.clarity: Four rules in the order a builder needs them (row, current pillar, file, places); the first screen at 1440 px shows no pillar icon, so a newcomer meets the drawings only after the opener.
reasons.brand_fidelity: The masters sit verbatim, the order never breaks, red appears only on the current icon from 48 px and never on Prussian, and the Track opener with "Watch the vote." reads as Oath & Action with the wordmark covered.
reasons.usefulness: Every size names its file, its token and the two-`<use>` markup, and the four places are listed with their sizes.
reasons.evidence_honesty: Each basis says design judgment or our measurements, and the opener's invented line carries Illustrative.
reasons.accessibility: The underline marks the current pillar at every size, `aria-current` carries it to screen readers, and the arrows are hidden from them; I did not run a screen reader.

items.to_ready: Ready as it stands. S1 is the one Should fix.

reasons.clarity: The class table and the five groups tell a builder where to look, though the class table's atlas example, Entrenched majority control, is the least legible drawing in the set at 48 px.
reasons.brand_fidelity: Red only standing alone or current, editions matched to surfaces with none red on Prussian, and the family reads as one hand from CL-001 to R-50.
reasons.usefulness: The list of 41 by ID, the inventory, the likeness test's command and the System 1 constants for encoding glyphs let a builder act without asking.
reasons.evidence_honesty: Labels follow DR-185, R-35 keeps Rejected, and the likeness figures say how they were measured; Rule 10.4's "a reviewer" leaves the actor unnamed.
reasons.accessibility: Every drawing sits beside its word and is hidden from screen readers, and each sheet's 124 meanings sit in one closed list, one Tab stop a category.

items.to_ready: Ready as it stands. Question 2 asks Dustin about pixel fits for the 37 symbols set at 24 px.

M1.what: The report reader prints its page heading over three empty gray bars standing in for text, which Master Brief section 6 rules out ("no grey boxes"), and cycles four headings through twelve pages.
M1.fix: Set two or three real lines of the report text under each heading, Illustrative like the rest of the piece, and give each of the twelve pages its own heading or make the report four pages long.

M2.what: The title "Most claims in these three chapters rest on the record" sits over bars where 17 of 39 claims are Documented, so the title claims a majority its chart does not show (H08).
M2.fix: Retitle to "Most claims in these three chapters are documented or well supported" (28 of 39), or change the invented counts so Documented holds a majority; update the alt to match.

S1.where: Chapter 09, `s-09-phone` and the phone row in `s-09-1-correct`
S1.what_and_fix: In the stacked 48 px column each down arrow follows its word, so the arrows sit at three x positions ("Explain ↓", "Track ↓", "Connect ↓") and point at nothing. Set each arrow in the icon column, centered under its icon between rows, or in one column at a fixed x after the longest word.

S2.what_and_fix: The atlas symbol example is CL-014 Entrenched majority control, whose fence, chamber, ballot and bar crowd into noise at 48 px. Use a variable that reads at 48 px, such as CL-009 Safe seats, Variable C1, which Rule 10.8 already shows.

S3.what_and_fix: The card's kicker reads "ACT" alone. Rule 01.21 lists "A pillar name alone" under "Never a kicker", and its label is "Act · How to take part", so the plate teaches a second fault it does not name. Set the kicker as "Act · How to take part" and keep the Public meeting drawing at 48 px beside its word, so the plate fails Rule 10.9 only.

S4.what_and_fix: An atlas ID prints as plain gray text ("Variable B3") while the "24 px" tag beneath it takes the boxed chip, so the size tag looks like the typed chip that Rules 10.6 and 10.8 draw for IDs. Box the atlas ID as Rules 10.6 and 10.8 do (D2-756), and set the 24 px tag as plain small text or a different form.

S5.what_and_fix: The headline breaks "The House hears the all- / party primary bill on March 3" at its hyphen, and the email error leaves "@," to open its second line. Set "all-party" with a non-breaking hyphen (U+2011), as D2-950 does for IDs, and rewrap the error message.

S6.what_and_fix: The Illustrative chip sits in the caption outside the plate, and the caption's second line hangs under it at the left edge. Put the chip at the head of the plate, as every other invented plate in the chapter does.

S7.where: Chapter 11, Rules 11.15 and 11.16, tokens and specifications
S7.what_and_fix: Both rules list `--oa-color-state-error-mark-on-newsprint` #E63946 while Rule 11.15 says the error mark draws in the text's ink and the token colors only the 4 px bar. A developer who reads the token list colors the mark red. Until Gate 2 settles the token's name (D2-880), label the line "the red bar" in both specifications and list `--oa-color-state-error-text-on-newsprint` as the mark's ink.
S7.owner: Chapter 11 hand, with the Engineer at Gate 2

S8.where: Chapter 11, Rule 11.1 and the six steps table
S8.what_and_fix: "Many state legislatures take testimony from the public there" prints no source. The research lead read five legislatures' own pages for this sentence (research notes of November 9, section 4, D2-423), and none appears in the chapter's sources. Add their source line after the Nebraska line.
S8.owner: Chapter 11 hand, with the Research lead

S9.where: Chapter 11, Rule 11.14, the live loop stepper, correct and failure
S9.what_and_fix: Its visible start text says "Press Play, or Next step to follow one link at a time." The editor's table fixes "link" in the alt only (D2-926). Make the visible text "one connection at a time" in both plates too.

S10.what_and_fix: On both covers the crop leaves a sliver of B's tail terminal, about 18 by 25 px, standing alone at the right edge, where it reads as a stray rectangle. Move B so the frame cuts the terminal off whole or keeps it whole, on both surfaces.

S11.what_and_fix: The Illustrative chip sits in the caption, where it opens the caption's sentence, while Rule 09.4's failure and Rule 12.1's failure carry it inside the plate under the band. Put it inside the plate.

S12.what_and_fix: The rule about the red target lists only `--oa-color-data-emphasis-on-newsprint` and `--oa-color-graphic-essential-on-newsprint`, both #121212. Add the red's token, `--oa-color-data-emphasis-red-on-newsprint` (#E63946), to the tokens and to the "Target weight" specification.

S13.what_and_fix: "How safe seats move the real choice to the primary" and "Nebraska has one chamber, so a bill's fifth step never comes" are headlines of pieces that do not exist, and neither carries Illustrative. Rule 01.21's plate labels each invented headline, so these take the label too.

S14.what_and_fix: "Source for the count" runs to 17 lines and holds the method, Ohio's vote, Missouri's figures and Utah's exclusion. Keep the source line to H04's order (publisher, title, period, geography, retrieved, the one qualification), and move "We counted each map..." with Ohio, Missouri and Utah into a short note headed "How we counted" under it, with every fact kept as DR-187 sets it.

S15.what_and_fix: Its label reads "On a section opener that serves Track, at 48 px", while Rule 09.4 puts the icon on a section opener at 128 px. Call the row "On a page that serves Track, at 48 px", matching chapter 09's "A section that serves Track".

S16.what_and_fix: At 1440 px the first screen of "Pillar icons" and of "Topic and atlas symbols" shows no drawing; the first one appears after the index. At the shell's last pass, allow an opener figure under the intro, and set the pillar row in 09 and a strip of a library sheet in 10.
